page: Microsoft Azure FX16-8mds_v2 is a constrained-vCPU instance within the FXmdsv2 compute- and memory-intensive family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It is provisioned with 4 dedicated physical cores supporting 2 threads per core, presenting 8 vCPUs alongside an expansive 260 MB L3 cache. Memory allocation is exceptionally dense at 336.0 GB of RAM, equating to 42.0 GB per vCPU. Local scratch capacity is bundled via a 945 GB NVMe SSD, and the platform supports Premium Storage. No discrete GPUs are present.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded compute, driven by the 4.2 GHz clock rate. The instance registered a Geekbench single-core score of 2165.0 (top 25%) and achieved top-tier performance in Geekbench text processing at 2931.0. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 34.31 GB/sec. In multi-threaded execution, the 8 vCPUs delivered a Geekbench multi-core score of 7546.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 8882.55, placing it in the middle tier. Memory subsystem testing logged a cached small-block read bandwidth of 691.15 GB/sec, though the PassMark memory score ranked in the bottom 25% at 1324.99.

The constrained CPU configuration offers high qualitative cost efficiency for software licensed on a per-core basis that requires massive memory allocations and high single-core frequency. Instead of licensing a full 16-core socket, workloads leverage 8 active vCPUs backed by 336.0 GB of RAM. Tradeoffs include limited overall multi-threaded throughput compared to full-core instances and weak generation speeds on medium-sized LLM models (8.54 tokens/sec).

With its high memory-to-core ratio, fast per-core execution, and integrated 945 GB NVMe SSD, the FX16-8mds_v2 is well configured for in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), relational databases with per-core licensing constraints, and memory-heavy batch data transformation.
description: Microsoft Azure FX16-8mds_v2 is a specialized instance designed for workloads requiring a very high memory-to-CPU ratio alongside high single-core frequency. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocking at 4.2 GHz, it allocates 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, complemented by a substantial 260 MB L3 cache, 336.0 GB of RAM (42.0 GB per vCPU), and a local 945 GB NVMe SSD. Single-core throughput is strong, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2165.0 and top-tier text processing performance. Multi-core compute and PassMark memory benchmarks align with average or lower-tier ratings due to the reduced core count. By constraining active vCPUs while retaining a heavy 336.0 GB memory footprint, this instance provides cost advantages for per-core licensed enterprise software, in-memory databases, and high-frequency analytical batch processing.
